acafly.habitat: Shaded ravines, creek bottoms and swamp forest in summer.
acafly.look: Listen for the explosive 'peet-sah' from the understory along streams; the nest hangs from a low beech or hemlock branch.

afcdov1.habitat: Suburbs; escapes that mix with Eurasian Collared-Doves.
afcdov1.look: Paler and smaller than Eurasian Collared-Dove, with a different, laughing call; study calls closely.

aldfly.habitat: Wet thickets and shrubby edges in migration.
aldfly.look: Only safely identified by voice: a burry 'free-beer'. Check willow and alder thickets in late May.

allhum.habitat: Winter feeders; very rare and hard to separate from Rufous.
allhum.look: A Rufous-type hummingbird at a winter feeder; confirmation usually needs a bander.

ambduc.habitat: Wooded swamps, beaver ponds and secluded marshes, usually with Mallards.
ambduc.look: Pick through Mallard flocks for a uniformly dark body with a paler head and an olive-yellow bill; in flight the underwing flashes white.

ameavo.habitat: Shallow coastal impoundments and lagoons; rare inland.
ameavo.look: Flocks sweeping upturned bills through shallow water; scan impoundments and coastal ponds in winter.

amebit.habitat: Freshwater marshes with dense cattails and wet meadows.
amebit.look: Walk dike edges slowly and scan the cattail edge for a streaked brown heron frozen with bill pointed up; most often seen when it flies between patches.

amecro.habitat: Everywhere: fields, towns, woods and roadsides.
amecro.look: Big roosts in winter; follow mobbing crows to roosting owls.

amegfi.look: Bouncing flight with 'po-ta-to-chip' calls; thistle feeders in winter.

amekes.habitat: Open fields, pastures, airports; perches on wires.
amekes.look: Small falcon on roadside wires bobbing its tail, or hovering over a field.

ameoys.habitat: Shell bars, oyster beds and beaches on the coast.
ameoys.look: Scan exposed shell rakes at low tide; the heavy orange bill is visible far away. Roosts on sandbars at high tide.

amepip.habitat: Plowed fields, sod farms, mudflats and reservoir shores in winter.
amepip.look: Scan bare fields for slim brown birds walking and bobbing their tails; flocks flush with 'pi-pit' calls.

amered.habitat: Deciduous woods, edges and thickets; common in migration.
amered.look: Watch for a bird constantly fanning its tail and wings to flush insects in mid-level foliage.

amerob.habitat: Lawns, parks, woods and berry trees; huge winter roosts.
amerob.look: Everywhere on lawns; in winter check holly and cedar stands for feeding flocks with waxwings.

amewig.habitat: Lakes, ponds, golf-course water and nearby lawns where they graze.
amewig.look: Listen for the whistled three-note call; flocks graze on grass near water and steal from diving coots.

amewoo.habitat: Wet thickets and young woods by day; fields and clearings at dusk in late winter.
amewoo.look: Visit a brushy field edge at dusk from January to March and listen for the nasal 'peent' and the twittering display flight.

amgplo.habitat: Sod farms, plowed fields and airports in fall; rarely on beaches.
amgplo.look: Scan turf farms in September and October for a slim plover with a bold eyebrow among Killdeer.

amhgul1.habitat: Beaches, landfills, large reservoirs and dams in winter.
amhgul1.look: The large pink-legged gull; study its plumages to pick out rarer large gulls among them.

amwpel.habitat: Large reservoirs, coastal lagoons and estuaries in winter.
amwpel.look: Flocks of enormous white birds fishing cooperatively in shallow bays, or soaring in spirals at midday.

anhing.habitat: Swamps, cypress ponds, lake edges and canals.
anhing.look: Look for a dark bird drying spread wings on a snag over water, or soaring high with a long tail; swims with only the head above water.

annhum.habitat: Feeders in winter; a very rare stray.
annhum.look: A large, stocky hummingbird at a winter feeder; the male's rose crown is distinctive.

anpswi.habitat: Caribbean species; extreme rarity in Florida.
anpswi.look: Small swift with a white rump over palms and open areas; needs photos.

arcter.habitat: Offshore; a rare migrant seen on pelagic trips or after storms.
arcter.look: Compare with Common Tern: shorter bill, longer tail, translucent wings; very rare from shore.

astfly.habitat: Dry brushy edges and open woods; a rare late-fall stray.
astfly.look: A pale Myiarchus in November and December; listen for the 'ka-brick' call and check tail pattern.

audshe.habitat: Gulf Stream waters; onshore after storms.
audshe.look: Pelagic trips or post-storm beach walks; a small black-and-white shearwater with fluttery flight.

babwar.habitat: Treetops in migration, especially in pines and oaks in fall.
babwar.look: Pick through fall mixed flocks for a plump, greenish warbler with buffy flanks and dark legs; in spring look for the chestnut sides.

bacspa.habitat: Open longleaf pine with wiregrass, recently burned; also clearcuts.
bacspa.look: Listen in April and May for a clear whistle followed by a trill from a low perch in open pine; nearly impossible to find when silent.

bahgoo.habitat: Park ponds with domestic waterfowl; an escape, not a wild bird.
bahgoo.look: Pale gray goose with two black bars across the back of the head, usually tame and with other geese.

bahswa.habitat: Bahamian species; an extreme rarity in South Florida.
bahswa.look: A Tree Swallow-like bird with a deeply forked tail among swallow flocks in the Keys; needs photos.

baisan.habitat: Dry margins of reservoirs, sod farms and upper beaches in fall.
baisan.look: Look above the waterline for a long-winged peep with scaly buff upperparts, usually in August and September.

baleag.habitat: Lakes, reservoirs, rivers and coasts; nests in tall pines near water.
baleag.look: Scan tall shoreline trees for a white head; nests are huge and reused each winter. Reservoir dams and fish-kill areas draw them.

balori.habitat: Tall deciduous trees, especially along rivers; winters at feeders in the South.
balori.look: Listen for rich whistled phrases from the tops of tall trees in spring; in winter offer grape jelly and oranges.

banswa.habitat: Sand and gravel pits with vertical banks; over lakes in migration.
banswa.look: Check swallow flocks over reservoirs in late summer for a small brown swallow with a clean breast band; colonies in sand banks.

barpet.habitat: Gulf Stream waters; occasionally blown inland by hurricanes.
barpet.look: After tropical systems, scan reservoirs and lakes for small dark seabirds; most are identified from photos.

barswa.habitat: Bridges, barns, open fields and water.
barswa.look: Fork-tailed swallows sweeping low over fields; nests of mud under bridges and eaves.

batpig1.habitat: Western forests; a very rare stray in the East.
batpig1.look: A large gray pigeon with a white nape crescent and yellow bill, usually at a feeder or in oaks.

bawwar.habitat: Deciduous and mixed woods; creeps on trunks and limbs.
bawwar.look: Watch large limbs and trunks for a striped bird moving like a nuthatch; the song is a thin squeaky wheel.

bbwduc.habitat: Shallow freshwater ponds, flooded fields, golf-course lakes and retention ponds, often near trees.
bbwduc.look: Listen for the high whistling calls in flight, often at dusk; by day they loaf in tight flocks on banks or perch in trees and on nest boxes.
bbwduc.time: Dusk and first light; loafing flocks any time

bcnher.habitat: Marsh edges, lake shores, mangroves; roosts by day in dense trees.
bcnher.look: Watch at dusk as hunched gray herons leave roost trees; listen for the loud 'quok' overhead after dark. By day scan dense shoreline trees.

belkin1.habitat: Rivers, lake shores, ponds and coastal creeks with perches over water.
belkin1.look: Listen for the loud rattle; scan wires and snags over water, and sandy banks for nest holes in spring.

belvir.habitat: Dense low thickets; a very rare migrant in the East.
belvir.look: A drab, small vireo moving quickly through brush with a husky jumbled song; needs careful notes.

bewwre.habitat: Brushy farmland and woodland edges; now extremely rare in the East.
bewwre.look: A long-tailed wren with a white eyebrow in brush piles; any Eastern sighting needs documentation.

bkbcuc.habitat: Wooded edges and thickets in migration.
bkbcuc.look: Secretive; look for the red eye ring and small tail spots when a cuckoo flies across an opening. Most likely in May and September.

bkbplo.habitat: Beaches, mudflats and sod farms; inland on reservoir shores and turf farms in migration.
bkbplo.look: Stands upright on open flats; check sod farms and drawn-down reservoirs in fall. The black axillaries show in flight.

bkbwar.habitat: Hemlocks and tall hardwoods in the mountains in summer; canopy in migration.
bkbwar.look: Look at the very tops of tall trees in May for a flaming orange throat; the song is a very high, thin trill.

bkchum.habitat: Feeders in winter; a rare western stray.
bkchum.look: A wintering hummingbird at a feeder that is maintained through December; tail-pumping while hovering is a clue.

bkhgro.habitat: Feeders in winter; a rare western stray.
bkhgro.look: A grosbeak with an orange breast and streaked flanks at a sunflower feeder in winter; compare carefully with young Rose-breasted.

bkhgul.habitat: Coastal waters and sewage ponds; a rare winter stray among Bonaparte's Gulls.
bkhgul.look: Scan Bonaparte's flocks for a slightly larger bird with a red bill and dark underwing primaries.

bkhpar.habitat: Suburbs and parks along Florida's Gulf coast; feral and established.
bkhpar.look: Flocks of green parakeets with black heads screeching over St. Petersburg and Fort Myers; roosts in palms.

bklkit.habitat: Open ocean; onshore after winter storms.
bklkit.look: Scan from piers after strong onshore winds in winter for a buoyant gull with solid black wingtips and a dark collar on young birds.

bknsti.habitat: Shallow impoundments, salt pans and flooded fields.
bknsti.look: Long pink legs wading in shallow water; noisy and conspicuous at any shallow pool in spring and summer.

bkpwar.habitat: Treetops in migration, mostly in May in the East.
bkpwar.look: Listen for the extremely high, even trill from the canopy in mid-May; in fall rare in the Southeast interior, more on the coast.

bkwvir.habitat: Mangroves and coastal hammocks of South Florida in summer.
bkwvir.look: Listen for a Red-eyed-like song with shorter phrases in mangroves from April to August; look for the dark whisker.

blbrol1.look: A brilliant roller on a wire or snag; captive origin.

blksco2.habitat: Ocean surf and inlets; reservoirs after storms.
blksco2.look: Scan scoter flocks for an all-dark duck with a yellow-orange bill knob; the most likely scoter on big inland lakes in late fall.

blkski.habitat: Sandy beaches, inlets and coastal lagoons.
blkski.look: Roosts in tight flocks on sandbars by day; at dusk watch them skim calm water with the lower bill slicing the surface.
blkski.time: Dusk and dawn for feeding; midday roosts

blkswa.habitat: Ornamental ponds; an escape from collections.
blkswa.look: Black swan with a red bill, usually tame and alone on a park lake.

blkter.habitat: Lakes, reservoirs and coastal waters in late summer migration.
blkter.look: Small dark tern with buoyant, erratic flight low over water; check reservoirs in August and after storms.

blkvul.habitat: Open country, roadsides, landfills; roosts on towers and dead trees.
blkvul.look: Short-tailed vulture with quick flaps; gathers at carcasses and communal roosts.

blugrb1.habitat: Overgrown fields, hedgerows, powerline cuts and brushy edges.
blugrb1.look: Listen for a rich, husky warble from a wire or shrub top in May; the heavy bill and rusty wing bars show on the brown female too.

blujay.habitat: Oak woods, suburbs, parks and feeders.
blujay.look: Loud and obvious; mobbing calls often lead to an owl or hawk.

bnhcow.habitat: Fields, feeders, pastures and woodland edges.
bnhcow.look: In flocks with other blackbirds; watch for females lurking near songbird nests in spring.

bnhnut.habitat: Pine stands, especially mature loblolly and longleaf.
bnhnut.look: Listen for squeaky-toy calls from the tops of pines; small groups move through pine crowns with chickadees.

boboli.habitat: Hayfields and grassy marsh in migration; rice fields in fall.
boboli.look: Listen for 'pink' calls overhead and watch for flocks dropping into tall grass in May and September; males are striking in spring.

bongul.habitat: Large lakes, dam tailwaters and coastal inlets in winter.
bongul.look: Small graceful gulls feeding like terns over water below dams and at lake outflows; flocks appear from November.

botgra.habitat: Salt marsh, beaches, coastal towns and inland lakes in Florida.
botgra.look: Noisy, long-tailed grackles displaying on marsh edges and parking lots; the females are brown.

brant.habitat: Coastal bays, mudflats and eelgrass beds; inland a rare storm-blown stray on reservoirs.
brant.look: A small dark goose with a white neck patch; scan coastal flats at low tide and reservoirs after coastal storms.

brdowl.habitat: Swamps, river bottoms and mature wooded neighborhoods.
brdowl.look: Listen for 'who cooks for you' at dusk; often answers an imitation. Check the dark side of trunks in big hardwoods by day.

brebla.habitat: Feedlots, parking lots and fields; a rare winter visitor in the East.
brebla.look: Pick through blackbird flocks at cattle lots for a yellow-eyed male without rusty edges and a plain gray female.

briter1.habitat: Offshore Gulf Stream waters; onshore after storms.
briter1.look: Pelagic trips off the Carolinas in summer, or beaches after hurricanes; a brown-backed tern with a white collar.

brnboo.habitat: Coastal waters, buoys and channel markers; increasingly regular in Florida.
brnboo.look: Scan navigation markers and piers for a dark booby with a white belly perched in plain view.

brncre.habitat: Mature woods with large rough-barked trunks in winter.
brncre.look: Watch tree trunks for a bark-colored bird spiraling up from the base and dropping to the next tree; the song is a high thin whisper.

brnnod.habitat: Dry Tortugas colonies; a storm stray elsewhere.
brnnod.look: A dark tern with a pale cap on a beach or pier after a hurricane.

brnowl.habitat: Farmland, marshes and open country; roosts in barns, silos and palms.
brnowl.look: Listen at night for a harsh, drawn-out screech; check old barns, church towers and palm crowns for roosting birds and pellets.

brnpel.habitat: Beaches, piers, inlets and offshore waters.
brnpel.look: Lines gliding inches above the waves; dramatic plunge dives near piers.

brnthr.habitat: Brushy edges, thickets, hedgerows and yards with dense shrubs.
brnthr.look: Sings doubled phrases from an exposed treetop in spring; otherwise rummages in leaf litter under shrubs.

brocow.habitat: Feedlots, lawns and feeders in Florida; a rare visitor.
brocow.look: A heavy cowbird with a thick neck ruff and red eye among Brown-headed Cowbirds.

brwhaw.habitat: Deep deciduous woods in summer; migrates in kettles over ridges in September.
brwhaw.look: Visit a hawk watch in the third week of September on a north-west wind; in summer listen for the thin whistle in mature forest.
brwhaw.time: Late morning to early afternoon on hawk-watch days

btbwar.habitat: Rhododendron and mountain laurel understory in the mountains; low shrubs in migration.
btbwar.look: Listen for the lazy 'I'm so lazeee' buzz from the understory; the male is unmistakable, the female shows a white wing spot.

btnwar.habitat: Pines and hemlocks in migration and in the mountains; cypress in the Coastal Plain.
btnwar.look: Listen for the buzzy 'zee-zee-zee-zoo-zee' from mid-canopy; one of the easiest warblers to find by song.

btywar.habitat: Western species; a rare fall and winter stray to feeders and oaks.
btywar.look: Check mixed flocks in late fall for a gray warbler with a black-and-white face and a yellow spot before the eye.

bubsan.habitat: Sod farms, airports and dry short grass in fall.
bubsan.look: Walk sod farms in late August and September looking for a buffy, dove-faced sandpiper with yellow legs among Killdeer and plovers.

bucpar.look: Long-tailed green parakeet with a blue crown, in small noisy flocks.

budger.habitat: Suburbs; escapes, once feral on Florida's Gulf coast.
budger.look: A small parakeet, often blue or yellow, with House Sparrows or at a feeder.

buffle.habitat: Lakes, reservoirs, bays and larger ponds.
buffle.look: Small black-and-white duck that dives constantly; scan sheltered coves and marinas. The white head patch catches the eye.

bufpar.look: Amazon with a turquoise forehead among mixed parrot flocks at roosts.

buggna.habitat: Deciduous woods, swamp edges and oak scrub.
buggna.look: Tiny, long-tailed gray bird constantly flicking its tail in the canopy edge; wheezy, scolding calls.

buhvir.habitat: Mixed pine-hardwood forest in winter and migration; mountains in summer.
buhvir.look: Sweet, slow phrases from mid-canopy; in winter forages with chickadee flocks in pines and oaks.

bulori.habitat: Feeders in winter; a rare western stray.
bulori.look: Check wintering orioles at feeders for a bird with an orange face and black eyeline; female needs careful study.

burowl.habitat: Short-grass fields, airports, vacant lots and golf courses in Florida.
burowl.look: Look for a small owl standing at a burrow mouth in mowed grass, often marked with a perch stake; Cape Coral has many.

buwtea.habitat: Shallow marshes, flooded fields, pond edges with mud and emergent vegetation.
buwtea.look: Small ducks tucked along muddy margins; scan the shallow ends of ponds and any flooded field during migration (March to April, August to October).

buwwar.habitat: Overgrown fields and brushy edges in summer; thickets in migration.
buwwar.look: Listen for the two-note 'bee-buzz' from a shrub top in spring; look for a yellow warbler with a black eyeline.

cacgoo1.habitat: Wherever Canada Geese gather: lawns, fields, reservoirs.
cacgoo1.look: Pick through Canada Goose flocks for a noticeably smaller bird with a short neck, steep forehead and stubby bill; compare directly with neighbors.

calhum.look: Tiny short-billed hummingbird at a feeder kept up through winter; often needs banding to confirm.

camwar.habitat: Spruce in summer; in migration conifers, flowering trees and sapsucker wells.
camwar.look: In spring check pines and flowering oaks for a streaked warbler with a chestnut cheek; in fall look in pines and at fruit.

cangoo.habitat: Lakes, ponds, golf courses, parks and fields; everywhere there is grass near water.
cangoo.look: Unmissable on lawns and shorelines; flocks fly in V formations between roost water and feeding fields.

canvas.habitat: Deep lakes and reservoirs; in the Southeast scarce and local in winter.
canvas.look: Scan big rafts of diving ducks for a long, sloping profile with a white body and chestnut head; often far from shore, so use a scope.

canwar.habitat: Dense shrub layers in moist woods and rhododendron in the mountains; low thickets in migration.
canwar.look: Look low in shady tangles in May and late August for a gray warbler with a yellow breast and black necklace; the song is a rich jumble.

carchi.look: Leads mixed flocks in winter; follow the chickadees to find warblers and kinglets.

carwre.habitat: Yards, brush piles, woods and porches everywhere.
carwre.look: The loud 'tea-kettle' song all year; investigates garages and flowerpots.

caster1.habitat: Large reservoirs, rivers and coastal waters.
caster1.look: The biggest tern, with a thick red bill; listen for the harsh heron-like call. Scan reservoir dams and sandbars in migration.

categr1.habitat: Pastures with livestock, mowed fields and roadside grass.
categr1.look: White egrets following cattle or tractors; evening flights to roosts.

cavswa.habitat: Bridges and culverts in Florida; a fall stray along the Atlantic coast.
cavswa.look: Check Cliff Swallow colonies and swallow flocks in November for a pale-throated, buffy-rumped swallow.

cedwax.habitat: Berry trees and shrubs: hollies, cedars, privet, hackberry; also over water catching insects.
cedwax.look: Listen for high thin lisps overhead; scan the tops of fruiting trees for tight flocks that arrive and strip a tree.

cerwar.habitat: Tall mature deciduous forest on ridges and river bluffs.
cerwar.look: Listen for a buzzy rising song from the very top of tall oaks in late April; craning upward is the only way.

chispa.habitat: Lawns with pines, yards, parks and fields.
chispa.look: Dry trill from a pine; winter flocks on lawns and field edges.

chiswi.habitat: Over towns, rivers and woods; roosts in chimneys.
chiswi.look: Cigar-shaped birds twittering overhead; in September watch a large chimney at sunset as hundreds funnel in to roost.

chswar.habitat: Shrubby regrowth, clearcuts and edges in migration and in the mountains.
chswar.look: Listen for 'pleased-pleased-pleased-to-MEETCHA' from young growth; in fall a lime-green bird with a gray face and white eye ring.

chwwid.habitat: Pine and oak woods with openings, especially in the Coastal Plain.
chwwid.look: Listen after dark for the loud 'chuck-will's-WIDOW'; drive quiet back roads with windows down and watch for eyeshine on the road.
chwwid.time: First hour after dark, before dawn

cintea.habitat: Shallow freshwater marshes; a rare stray in the East, usually with Blue-winged Teal.
cintea.look: Check Blue-winged Teal flocks for a rusty-red drake; females are nearly identical to Blue-winged, so focus on drakes.

clarai11.look: Listen for clattering calls across the marsh; watch creek edges and openings at low tide and at high spring tides when birds are pushed to the edges.
clarai11.time: Low tide and extreme high tides

clcspa.habitat: Weedy edges and brushy fields in fall; a rare migrant.
clcspa.look: Pick through Chipping Sparrow flocks in October for a buffy sparrow with a pale lore and brown rump.

cliswa.habitat: Bridges and dams over large rivers and reservoirs.
cliswa.look: Look under highway bridges over big water for colonies of gourd-shaped mud nests; square tail and pale rump in flight.

cockat.look: A crested gray-and-yellow parrot calling from a yard tree; escaped.

cogdov.habitat: Sandy open ground, pine edges, coastal scrub and dirt roads.
cogdov.look: Tiny dove walking on bare sand; flushes low showing rusty wings. Walk sandy tracks and scan field edges.

comeid.habitat: Ocean inlets, jetties and rocky coast; a rare winter visitor south of the Carolinas.
comeid.look: Scan jetties and inlet mouths for a large, heavy duck riding the swell; young birds are brown and easy to pass over.

comgal1.habitat: Ponds and marshes with lily pads and emergent plants.
comgal1.look: Swims openly along edges, flicking its white tail; noisy clucks from the reeds.

comgol.habitat: Large reservoirs, rivers below dams and coastal bays.
comgol.look: Scan deep open water and dam tailwaters; the drake's round white cheek spot and bright white body stand out among scaup.

comgra.habitat: Lawns, parking lots, fields and feeders.

comloo.habitat: Large reservoirs and coastal waters from November to April.
comloo.look: Scan open water from dams and boat ramps for a large, low diver; in late March listen for yodeling before they leave.

commer.habitat: Large clear rivers, reservoirs and dam tailwaters.
commer.look: Long, low white-bodied duck on cold rivers; scan fast water below dams and open lake arms in midwinter.

commyn.habitat: Shopping-center parking lots, fast-food lots and gas stations in Florida.
commyn.look: Look for a chunky brown bird with a yellow bill and eye patch walking under cars and on signs; nests in letters of store signs. Flashes white wing patches in flight.

comnig.habitat: Open country, gravel rooftops, pine flats; migrates over towns in late summer.
comnig.look: Watch the sky at dusk for long-winged, erratic fliers with white wing bars; listen for the nasal 'peent'. Late August evenings bring flocks.

compea.habitat: Neighborhoods and parks with feral flocks, especially in Florida.
compea.look: Unmistakable; listen for the loud wailing calls and check rooftops and lawns in known neighborhoods.

comrav.habitat: Mountains, cliffs and increasingly Piedmont towers and landfills.
comrav.look: Scan ridgelines and quarry walls for a huge, wedge-tailed corvid with a croaking call; also check cell towers in the foothills.

comter.habitat: Beaches, inlets and large reservoirs in migration.
comter.look: Check tern flocks on sandbars and reservoir shores in May and August to September; dark wedge in the outer wing.

comyel.habitat: Marshes, wet thickets, weedy ditches and brushy fields.
comyel.look: The 'witchity-witchity' song from low cover; pishing brings the masked male up briefly.

conwar.habitat: Dense weedy ground cover and thickets in fall migration; very secretive.
conwar.look: Walk slowly through dense goldenrod and jewelweed in late September and watch the ground for a large, walking warbler with a complete eye ring.

coohaw.habitat: Suburbs, woodlots and parks; nests in tall pines and oaks.
coohaw.look: Watch feeders and dove flocks for a long-tailed hawk; listen for the cackling call near nests in spring.

corshe1.look: Pelagic trips in summer and fall; from shore only during strong onshore winds or after storms.

cursan.habitat: Coastal flats; a very rare visitor from Eurasia.
cursan.look: Check Dunlin flocks for a longer-legged, cleaner bird with a white rump; needs documentation.

daejun.habitat: Woodland edges, yards and feeders in winter; mountain forests in summer.
daejun.look: Flocks on the ground under feeders and along edges flashing white outer tail feathers.

dickci.habitat: Hayfields and weedy fields; a sporadic breeder and rare migrant.
dickci.look: Listen for 'dick-dick-ciss-ciss' from a weed stalk in a big hayfield in June; in winter check House Sparrow flocks at feeders.

doccor.habitat: Lakes, rivers, reservoirs, coastal waters; perches on snags and buoys.
doccor.look: Lines of dark birds flying low over water; large roosts on dead trees and channel markers.

dowwoo.habitat: Woods, edges and yards; often in mixed flocks.
dowwoo.look: Small woodpecker working thin branches with chickadees and titmice.

dunlin.habitat: Tidal flats and beaches in winter; occasionally reservoir shores inland.
dunlin.look: Hunched gray shorebirds with drooping bills in large winter flocks on flats.

eargre.habitat: Lakes, sewage ponds and bays; rare in the East.
eargre.look: Pick through Horned Grebe flocks for a peaked head, dusky cheek and thin upturned bill.

easblu.habitat: Open fields with scattered trees, golf courses, pastures and nest boxes.
easblu.look: Scan wires and fence posts along fields; soft warbling calls in flight.

easkin.habitat: Open fields, pond edges, orchards and wires in summer.
easkin.look: Perches upright on fences and wires, chasing insects and crows; the white tail tip is diagnostic.

easmea.look: Scan fence posts for a chunky bird with a yellow breast; the slurred whistle carries across fields.

easowl1.habitat: Wooded suburbs, parks and woodlots with cavities.
easowl1.look: Listen after dark for the descending whinny and soft trill; check wood duck boxes and cavity entrances on cold sunny afternoons.

easpho.habitat: Bridges, barns, creek banks and open woodland edges.
easpho.look: Perches low, pumping its tail; nests under bridges and eaves. Says its name.

eastow.look: Loud scratching in leaves and the 'drink-your-tea' song; perches up when pished.

easwpw1.habitat: Dry deciduous and mixed woods with open understory.
easwpw1.look: Listen on still spring nights for the endless 'whip-poor-will'; most reliable in the hills on moonlit nights.

eawpew.habitat: Open deciduous and mixed woods with a mid-level understory.
eawpew.look: Listen for the slurred 'pee-a-wee' through the heat of the day; it sallies from a mid-height perch and returns to the same spot.

eawvir1.habitat: Tall riverside trees such as sycamores and cottonwoods.
eawvir1.look: Listen for a rapid warbling song from the tops of big riverside trees in May; plain gray-and-white vireo.

egygoo.habitat: Golf courses, retention ponds and lawns in Florida suburbs.
egygoo.look: Tan goose with a chocolate eye patch, grazing on grass near water, usually in pairs or family groups; loud and conspicuous.

eleter1.habitat: Pacific species; a very rare stray among Royal and Sandwich Terns.
eleter1.look: Pick through coastal tern roosts for a slimmer, orange-billed tern with a long drooping crest; needs photos.

eucdov.habitat: Towns, farmyards, grain stores and suburban wires.
eucdov.look: Pale dove with a black neck collar on wires and rooftops; listen for the three-note coo.

eursta.habitat: Towns, farms and fields; huge winter roosts.
eursta.look: Everywhere; check flocks for blackbirds mixed in.

eurwig.habitat: Lakes and ponds; a rare winter stray among American Wigeon.
eurwig.look: Scan wigeon flocks for a drake with a rusty head and buff forehead and gray flanks; compare head color carefully in good light.

evegro.habitat: Feeders and box elders in irruption winters; very rare in the Southeast.
evegro.look: A huge-billed yellow finch at a sunflower feeder in an invasion year; listen for loud 'peer' calls overhead.

fiespa.habitat: Old fields with scattered saplings and briars.
fiespa.look: The accelerating bouncing-ball song from an overgrown field; pink bill and plain face.

fiscro.habitat: Rivers, lakes, coasts and increasingly towns and parking lots.
fiscro.look: Separate from American Crow by the nasal 'uh-uh' call; flocks near water and fast-food lots.

flsjay.habitat: Low oak scrub on sandy soil in central Florida; needs recently burned scrub.
flsjay.look: Visit managed scrub preserves at dawn; family groups perch on top of oaks and are often fearless. Listen for harsh calls.

forter.habitat: Lakes, reservoirs, marshes and coastal waters, especially in winter.
forter.look: Winter tern with a black ear patch; scan reservoirs and marsh channels for terns diving for small fish.

fotfly.habitat: Open fields and wires; a rare but regular stray to Florida and the Atlantic coast.
fotfly.look: A black-capped flycatcher with impossibly long tail streamers on a fence or wire; most occur in fall.

foxspa.habitat: Brushy thickets and woodland edges in winter.
foxspa.look: Listen for loud two-footed scratching in dry leaves under shrubs; a big rusty sparrow often at brush piles after snow.

fragul.habitat: Sod farms, lakes and coastal flats; a rare migrant from the prairies.
fragul.look: Check Laughing and Ring-billed Gull flocks in fall for a smaller, pinker-breasted gull with white eye crescents and a bold wingtip pattern.

fuwduc.habitat: Rice fields, wet prairie and shallow marshes with emergent plants; far less tied to trees than Black-bellied.
fuwduc.look: Scan flooded fields and marsh edges for a tawny duck standing tall; most often found by its whistled calls as flocks move at dawn and dusk.

gadwal.habitat: Ponds, lake coves and marshes with submerged vegetation.
gadwal.look: A plain gray duck with a black rear end and a white wing patch that shows when it stretches; often with wigeon and coots.

gbbgul.habitat: Beaches, inlets and landfills; rare inland.
gbbgul.look: A huge black-backed gull standing above the others at a coastal roost.

giwrai1.habitat: South American; an escape in Florida.
giwrai1.look: A huge rail walking marsh edges; any sighting is an escaped bird.

glagul.habitat: Landfills, beaches and reservoir roosts; a rare winter visitor.
glagul.look: Scan big gull roosts for a very pale, large gull with white wingtips, usually a first-winter bird.

gloibi.habitat: Freshwater marshes, flooded fields and impoundments.
gloibi.look: Dark ibis flocks feeding in shallow marsh; in good light the chestnut and green gloss shows.

gnwtea.habitat: Muddy pond edges, flooded fields and shallow marsh.
gnwtea.look: Tiny ducks packed along mudflats and shorelines; often overlooked, so scan margins slowly.

gockin.habitat: Pines, hemlocks and cedars in winter; spruce-fir in the mountains in summer.
gockin.look: Listen for very high thin 'see-see-see' from conifer tops; look up into pines where small birds hover at branch tips.

goleag.habitat: Mountain ridges and large reservoirs with waterfowl in winter; very rare.
goleag.look: Scan ridgelines on hawk-watch days in November and reservoir shores in winter for a huge dark eagle with a golden nape.

gowwar.habitat: Shrubby regrowth and old fields in the mountains in summer; woodland edges in migration.
gowwar.look: Listen for a buzzy 'bee-bzz-bzz-bzz' from young growth in May; in migration check mixed flocks for the yellow crown and black face.

gragoo.habitat: Park ponds and farm ponds; nearly all are domestic escapes.
gragoo.look: A heavy gray goose with an orange bill among park waterfowl; check the tame flocks at urban ponds.

graspa.habitat: Large grassy fields, hayfields and airports in summer; weedy fields in winter.
graspa.look: Listen for the insect-like buzz from a weed stalk or fence in spring; in winter walk broomsedge fields and watch for a flat-headed sparrow dropping in.

grbani.habitat: Brushy edges and fields; a rare fall stray from the west.
grbani.look: A loose black bird with a grooved bill in low shrubs or on fences, usually in late fall.

grbher3.habitat: Any water from creeks to coasts; also fields in winter.
grbher3.look: Everywhere; also hunts rodents in dry fields in winter.

grcfly.habitat: Deciduous and mixed woods with cavities; wooded suburbs.
grcfly.look: Listen for the rising 'wheep' from the canopy; it stays high, so look for a large flycatcher with a rusty tail at a cavity or snag.

grecor.habitat: Coastal jetties and pilings in winter; rare south of the Carolinas.
grecor.look: Scan cormorant roosts on jetties for a bulkier bird with a white throat and yellow chin patch.

greegr.habitat: Lake edges, marshes, flats and ditches.
greegr.look: Tall white egret standing motionless at the water's edge; easy anywhere there is shallow water.

grefla2.habitat: Shallow coastal lagoons and mudflats in South Florida.
grefla2.look: Scan wide shallow flats from a distance; a tall pink bird feeding with head upside down. Beware escaped zoo birds inland.

gresca.habitat: Large lakes and coastal bays; rarer inland than Lesser Scaup.
gresca.look: Pick through scaup rafts for rounder heads with a green gloss and a broader bill nail; identification needs close views.

greshe.habitat: Offshore waters in summer; onshore after storms.
greshe.look: After June and July storms scan beaches for a large brown shearwater with a dark cap; sometimes found exhausted on the sand.

greyel.habitat: Shallow pools, flooded fields, reservoir margins and tidal flats.
greyel.look: Wades actively, sometimes dashing after fish; the ringing three-note alarm call carries far.

grhowl.habitat: Woods with open country nearby, including suburbs.
grhowl.look: Listen on winter nights for deep hooting duets; at dusk watch tall snags and the tops of pines for a silhouette with ear tufts.
grhowl.time: Dusk and night, especially December to February

grnher.habitat: Wooded pond edges, creeks, docks and ditches.
grnher.look: Scan overhanging branches and dock pilings for a small hunched heron; flushes with a loud 'skeow'.

grwpel1.habitat: Old World species; an escape in Florida.
grwpel1.look: A huge pelican with pink skin around the eye among American White Pelicans; zoo origin.

grycat.habitat: Dense thickets, hedgerows and shrubby edges.
grycat.look: Listen for the cat-like mew from inside shrubs; it responds to pishing and perches briefly on top.

grykin.habitat: Coastal wires, mangroves and beach towns in Florida.
grykin.look: Big gray kingbird with a heavy bill and notched tail on coastal wires from April to September; loud 'pe-cheer-ry'.

gubter2.habitat: Salt marsh, coastal fields and impoundments.
gubter2.look: A stocky pale tern that hawks insects over marsh and fields rather than diving; black bill and gull-like flight.

gunhaw1.habitat: Cuban endemic; an astonishing stray to Florida.
gunhaw1.look: A Cooper's-like hawk in South Florida; only with thorough photos.

gwfgoo.habitat: Reservoirs, sod farms and agricultural fields, usually with Canada Geese.
gwfgoo.look: Look for a gray-brown goose with an orange bill, pink-orange legs and barred belly inside goose flocks; scan grazing flocks slowly from a distance.
gwfgoo.time: Morning and late afternoon on fields

gycthr.habitat: Shady woods and thickets in migration, mostly in May and October.
gycthr.look: A cold gray-brown thrush on the ground in dim understory; listen for the thin, nasal flight call at night and the 'queep' by day.

haiwoo.habitat: Mature forest with large trunks; less in suburbs.
haiwoo.look: Like a large Downy with a long bill; listen for the sharper 'peek' and look on big trunks in older woods.

helgui.habitat: Farmyards and suburban lots; free-ranging domestic birds.
helgui.look: Noisy spotted birds walking lawns and road edges in groups.

henspa.habitat: Weedy fields with dense grass and standing dead stems in winter; pine savanna.
henspa.look: Walk broomsedge and pine savanna in winter and watch for a flat-headed, olive-faced sparrow that flies low and dives in; rarely seen well.

herthr.habitat: Woodland understory, thickets and yards with berries in winter.
herthr.look: Watch leaf litter at wood edges for a thrush that raises and slowly lowers its rusty tail; soft 'chup' call.

hoomer.habitat: Wooded ponds, beaver swamps, creek mouths and quiet coves.
hoomer.look: Shy; approach cover slowly and scan the shaded back of small ponds. The drake's fan crest flashes white when raised.
hoomer.time: First and last hours of light

hooori.habitat: Palms and feeders; a rare winter stray.
hooori.look: An orange oriole with a black throat at a hummingbird or jelly feeder in winter; nests in palms where it is resident.

hoowar.habitat: Moist deciduous woods with a dense shrub layer, often near streams.
hoowar.look: Listen for the loud 'weeta-weeta-wee-tee-o' from the understory; it flashes white tail spots as it forages low.

horgre.habitat: Open water of reservoirs, lakes and bays in winter.
horgre.look: Scan open water for a small, pale grebe with a clean white cheek; often in loose groups away from shore. Scope from dams and boat ramps.

horlar.habitat: Bare plowed fields, sod farms and airports in winter.
horlar.look: Scan the barest fields for small brown birds walking, not hopping; often found by their tinkling flight calls overhead.

houfin.look: Common at feeders; the streaky red finch with a curved culmen.

houspa.habitat: Towns, farms, shopping centers and feeders.

houwre.habitat: Brushy yards, thickets and woodpiles; winters in dense tangles.
houwre.look: Bubbling song in spring in the Piedmont and mountains; in winter listen for a harsh chatter from brush piles.

hrshaw.habitat: Southwestern deserts; in the Southeast an escaped falconry bird.
hrshaw.look: A dark hawk with chestnut shoulders, often wearing jesses; report it but expect an escape.

indbun.habitat: Brushy fields, edges, powerline cuts and roadsides.
indbun.look: Sings paired phrases from wires and treetops all summer; in fall brown birds gather in weedy fields.

ivbwoo.habitat: Historically old-growth bottomland swamp; no accepted records in decades.
ivbwoo.look: Any report requires extraordinary evidence; a Pileated Woodpecker is the expected bird.

kenwar.habitat: Moist deciduous woods with dense low understory.
kenwar.look: Listen for the rolling 'tory-tory-tory' from the shrub layer in May; it walks on the ground under cover.

killde.habitat: Gravel lots, fields, pond edges, rooftops; anywhere open.
killde.look: Loud, obvious, everywhere; check any Killdeer flock for other plovers hidden with it.

kinrai4.habitat: Freshwater and brackish marshes with tall cattails and rushes.
kinrai4.look: Listen at dawn and dusk for the grunting 'kek-kek-kek' series; walk marsh edges quietly after rain when birds come to openings.

kirwar.habitat: Young jack pine in Michigan; in the Southeast only a rare migrant in scrub and pines.
kirwar.look: A large, tail-pumping gray-and-yellow warbler low in scrub or young pines in late April or October; needs photos.

laplon.habitat: Bare plowed fields and sod farms in winter, usually with Horned Larks.
laplon.look: Scan Horned Lark flocks in the barest fields for a chunkier bird with a rusty nape and rattling flight call.

larspa.habitat: Dry open fields and sandy roads; a rare migrant.
larspa.look: A large, boldly head-striped sparrow on bare ground in August and September; often with Chipping Sparrows.

laugul.habitat: Beaches, parking lots, inlets and piers on the coast; occasionally inland reservoirs.
laugul.look: The common dark-hooded gull of Southern beaches; noisy and tame around people.

lazbun.habitat: Feeders and weedy fields; a very rare western stray.
lazbun.look: Check Indigo Bunting flocks and feeders for a bird with a turquoise head, orange breast and white wing bars.

lbbgul.habitat: Beaches, reservoirs, landfills and sod farms in winter.
lbbgul.look: Pick through Herring and Ring-billed flocks for a slate-backed gull with yellow legs; increasing every year.

lcspet.look: Check beaches, inlets and even inland lakes in the day after a hurricane for a dark storm-petrel with bounding flight.

leabit.habitat: Cattail and bulrush marshes over water.
leabit.look: Listen for the soft cooing in spring; watch the reed edge from a dike for a tiny heron climbing stems or making short low flights.

leafly.habitat: Woodland edges, orchards and second growth in migration.
leafly.look: Small, big-headed Empidonax calling an emphatic 'che-BEK'; check edges in late April and September.

leasan.habitat: Muddy edges of ponds, ditches, flooded fields and flats.
leasan.look: The tiny brown peep with yellow legs on mud; often the only peep at small inland puddles.

leater1.habitat: Sandy beaches, dredge islands and gravel rooftops near water.
leater1.look: Tiny tern hovering and plunging in shallow water; noisy colonies on protected beaches April to August. Check large flat roofs near the coast.

lecspa.habitat: Dense broomsedge and damp grassy fields in winter; very secretive.
lecspa.look: Walk tall grass fields in winter and watch for a tiny orange-faced sparrow that flushes briefly and drops; rarely perches up.

lesnig.habitat: Open desert and scrub; a rare winter stray to South Florida.
lesnig.look: Low, floppy flight over fields at dusk; compare wing-patch position with Common Nighthawk.

lessca.habitat: Lakes, reservoirs, bays and large ponds.
lessca.look: Big rafts offshore on the largest water; note the peaked head with purple gloss. Scan from boat ramps and dams.

lesyel.habitat: Flooded fields, shallow pools and marsh edges.
lesyel.look: Slim, bright-yellow legs wading in shallow fresh water; compare bill length with Greater Yellowlegs when together.

libher.habitat: Freshwater marshes, ponds, ditches and tidal pools.
libher.look: Slate-blue heron stalking slowly; white immatures mix with Snowy Egrets, so check dull legs and two-tone bill.

licpar.habitat: South Florida suburbs; mixed with Red-crowned flocks.
licpar.look: Pick through amazon flocks for a maroon forehead and lilac crown; needs good light.

limpki.habitat: Freshwater swamps, lake shores and canals with apple snails.
limpki.look: Listen for the wailing scream at night and dawn; walk shorelines looking for a brown ibis-like bird probing the mud.

linspa.habitat: Brushy wet edges and weedy thickets in migration and winter.
linspa.look: Pick through sparrow flocks for a finely streaked, buffy-breasted bird that raises a slight crest; shy and quick to drop into cover.

litgul.habitat: Lakes, sewage ponds and coastal waters among Bonaparte's Gulls.
litgul.look: Pick through Bonaparte's Gull flocks for a tiny gull with dark underwings and rounded wingtips, usually in late winter.

lobcur.habitat: Coastal flats and beaches; a rare winter visitor in the Southeast.
lobcur.look: A huge sandpiper with an improbably long bill on open flats; most are in Florida.

lobdow.habitat: Freshwater pools and flooded fields, more than coastal flats.
lobdow.look: Check dowitcher flocks on fresh water in fall and winter; the sharp 'keek' call is the surest clue.

logshr.habitat: Open pastures with fences and scattered trees, airports, old fields.
logshr.look: Scan fence posts, wires and bare treetops for a gray masked bird; check thorny shrubs and barbed wire for impaled prey.

lotduc.habitat: Ocean inlets and large reservoirs in winter.
lotduc.look: Scan open water for a small, pale duck that dives often; listen for the yodeling calls of flocks offshore.

lotjae.habitat: Far offshore; onshore or on reservoirs only after storms, mostly in fall.
lotjae.look: A slim, tern-like jaeger; check reservoirs and beaches in the days after tropical systems in August and September.

louwat.habitat: Fast rocky streams in wooded ravines.
louwat.look: Walk a clear stream in March and April and listen for a loud ringing song that slurs downward; it bobs along the water's edge.

macwar.habitat: Western species; an extreme rarity in dense low thickets.
macwar.look: A skulking gray-hooded warbler with broken white eye arcs in low brush; needs photos to separate from Mourning.

magfri.habitat: Coastal skies, piers and fishing boats in Florida; inland after storms.
magfri.look: Look up: a huge black bird with angular wings hanging motionless over the coast, especially on hot afternoons and before storms.

magwar.habitat: Woodland edges and young conifers in migration.
magwar.look: Check low to mid-level edges in May and September for a yellow warbler with a black necklace and a white tail band.

mallar3.habitat: Any water, from park ponds to marshes.
mallar3.look: The default dabbling duck; check park flocks for wild-type birds and for other species hiding among them.

mancuc.habitat: Mangroves and tropical hammocks in South Florida.
mancuc.look: Very secretive; listen for the slow guttural call in the mangroves of Sanibel and the Keys, and watch for movement in dense canopy.

manduc.habitat: Park ponds; an escape from collections.
manduc.look: Ornate small duck with Wood Duck habits; look among Wood Ducks and park waterfowl.

margod.habitat: Tidal flats and beaches on the coast in winter.
margod.look: Big cinnamon-brown shorebird with a long upturned bill, often in roosting flocks on sandbars at high tide.

marwre.look: Listen for the gurgling, mechanical song from dense reeds; wait by an opening and it will climb a stem to look.

masboo.habitat: Tropical seas; nests in the Dry Tortugas, rare elsewhere.
masboo.look: A large white booby with a black mask on offshore markers or after storms; most records are Florida.

merlin.habitat: Open country, coasts and reservoirs in migration and winter.
merlin.look: A compact dark falcon rocketing low over flats or perched on a snag watching shorebird flocks; most frequent on the coast in fall.

miskit.habitat: Riverside woods, tall pines in towns, and open skies in summer.
miskit.look: Look up on summer afternoons for graceful gray kites catching dragonflies; neighborhoods with tall trees along rivers often have nesting pairs.

monpar.habitat: Suburbs, parks and utility structures with huge stick nests.
monpar.look: Find the bulky communal nests on poles and stadium lights; noisy flocks commute at dawn and dusk.

motduc.habitat: Florida marshes, ditches, retention ponds and wet prairie.
motduc.look: A dark Mallard-like duck in pairs; note the unmarked buffy face and yellow bill. Check roadside ditches and pond edges.

moudov.habitat: Fields, yards, wires and open woods everywhere.
moudov.look: Common on wires and the ground; whistling wings when it flushes.

mouwar.habitat: Dense low thickets and weedy tangles in migration.
mouwar.look: Very skulking; stand quietly by a dense tangle in late May or September and listen for a loud 'chek' and a rolling song.

musduc.habitat: Urban ponds and canals; feral birds, often tame.
musduc.look: Large dark duck with red facial warts, loafing on pond edges and parking lots near water.

mutswa.habitat: Park lakes and ponds, often introduced or feral.
mutswa.look: Huge white swan with an orange bill and black knob; check ornamental lakes and golf courses.

naswar.habitat: Woodland edges and thickets in migration.
naswar.look: Look for a gray-headed warbler with a white eye ring and yellow throat in mixed flocks in late April and October.

neocor.habitat: Lakes and coastal waters; a rare but increasing visitor.
neocor.look: Pick through cormorant roosts for a smaller, longer-tailed bird with a white edge to the pointed gular patch.

norbob.habitat: Weedy fields, pine savanna, brushy edges and recently burned or thinned woods.
norbob.look: Listen for the clear 'bob-WHITE' whistle from field edges in spring and summer; coveys flush explosively from grass. Walk slowly along brushy edges.

norcar.habitat: Thickets, yards, edges and feeders everywhere.
norcar.look: The first bird to sing before dawn; males on exposed perches in spring.

norfli.habitat: Open woods, edges, yards and fields; feeds on the ground.
norfli.look: Look for a brown woodpecker flushing from the ground with a white rump; loud 'wick-wick-wick' in spring.

norgan.habitat: Ocean waters within sight of shore in winter.
norgan.look: Scan from beaches and piers for large white birds plunging headfirst into the sea; onshore winds bring them close.

norhar2.habitat: Marshes, large fields and pastures in winter.
norhar2.look: Low, tilting flight over grass with the white rump flashing; scan big open fields at dawn and in the last light.

normoc.look: Sings from rooftops and wires, sometimes at night; flashes white wing patches.

norpar.habitat: Riverside and swamp forest with Spanish moss or beard lichen.
norpar.look: Listen for the rising buzz with a snap at the end from the canopy along rivers; small and high.

norpin.habitat: Shallow lakes, flooded fields and marshes.
norpin.look: Long-necked, elegant duck; scan the far edges of flooded fields and shallow bays where it tips up to feed.

norsho.habitat: Shallow ponds, sewage lagoons and marshes with rich surface food.
norsho.look: Look for groups swimming in circles with bills skimming the surface; the big spoon bill is obvious even at distance.

norwat.habitat: Swampy pools, slow creeks and wet thickets in migration.
norwat.look: Look at the muddy edges of woodland pools for a bobbing streaked warbler; the loud 'chink' call gives it away.

nrwswa.habitat: Creek banks, bridges, culverts and lake shores.
nrwswa.look: Brown swallow with a dingy throat flying low over water near bridges; nests in drainpipes and bank crevices.

nstspa.habitat: Salt marsh in winter; wet grassy fields in migration.
nstspa.look: Visit high marsh edges at extreme high tides in October to see sparrows pushed onto the wrack; an orange-faced, blurry-streaked bird.

nswowl.habitat: Dense conifers and rhododendron in the mountains; rare in winter elsewhere.
nswowl.look: Listen on spring nights at high elevations for the monotonous tooting; in winter check dense cedars and holly thickets for whitewash.

nutman.habitat: Weedy lots and grassy edges in South Florida; a small feral population.
nutman.look: Small brown finch with a scaled breast in flocks in seeding grass; Miami area.

olsfly.habitat: Tall dead snags above forest openings, burns and beaver ponds in migration.
olsfly.look: Scan the very top of the tallest dead tree at a woodland edge for an upright, vested flycatcher; listen for 'quick-three-beers' in May and September.

orcori.habitat: Open woodland edges, orchards and scattered trees near water in summer.
orcori.look: Listen for a fast, rich warble from treetops along field edges in May; the male is dark chestnut and easy to miss as a blackbird.

orcwar.habitat: Brushy thickets, hedgerows and weedy edges in winter.
orcwar.look: Scan low shrubs and thickets in winter for a dull yellow-olive warbler with faint streaks; often with kinglets and sparrows.

osprey.habitat: Lakes, reservoirs, rivers and coasts; nests on platforms and channel markers.
osprey.look: Watch over open water for a hovering raptor that plunges feet-first; nests on poles and markers are obvious in spring.

ovenbi1.habitat: Mature deciduous forest floor with deep leaf litter.
ovenbi1.look: Listen for the ringing 'teacher-teacher-TEACHER' from inside the woods; it walks the ground like a tiny chicken and sings from a low branch.

pacloo.habitat: Coastal waters and large reservoirs; very rare in the East.
pacloo.look: A compact loon with a rounded head and straight bill; compare carefully with Common and Red-throated. Needs photos.

paibun.habitat: Brushy coastal edges and maritime scrub in summer; feeders in Florida in winter.
paibun.look: Listen for a sweet warble from a shrub top near the coast in May; in winter offer white millet at Florida feeders.

palwar.habitat: Open ground: lawns, field edges, pond margins and pine flats in winter.
palwar.look: Look on the ground and in low shrubs for a warbler constantly pumping its tail; yellow undertail coverts.

parjae.habitat: Nearshore ocean, chasing terns and gulls; rare on large reservoirs after storms.
parjae.look: Watch tern flocks from piers and inlets in fall; a dark falcon-like bird harrying a tern until it drops its fish is a jaeger.

pecsan.habitat: Grassy wet fields, flooded sod and marsh edges.
pecsan.look: Look in wet grass rather than open mud for a peep with a sharply cut streaked breast; fall is best.

peflov.habitat: Suburbs; escaped pets, occasionally small feral groups.
peflov.look: Tiny green parrot with a peach face at a feeder or in a palm.

perfal.habitat: Cities, bridges, coasts and large reservoirs.
perfal.look: Scan tall buildings and bridge towers; on the coast watch shorebird flocks erupt. Fall migration peaks early October on the beach.

phivir.habitat: Woodland edges and young growth in fall migration.
phivir.look: Check mixed flocks in late September for a small yellow-breasted vireo with a dark loral line; easily passed off as Warbling.

pibgre.habitat: Ponds, marshes and lake coves with emergent vegetation.
pibgre.look: Small brown grebe that dives or sinks when watched; scan edges of ponds and listen for the cuckoo-like whooping in spring.

pilwoo.habitat: Mature forest, swamps and wooded suburbs with big dead trees.
pilwoo.look: Listen for loud wild laughter and slow heavy drumming; look for fresh rectangular holes low on trunks.

pinsis.habitat: Feeders, sweetgums and alders in irruption winters.
pinsis.look: Streaky little finch with yellow in the wings among goldfinch flocks; listen for the rising buzzy 'zreee'.

pinwar.habitat: Pine woods year-round; feeders in winter.
pinwar.look: Listen for a musical trill from pine tops; often the first warbler singing in February. Takes suet at feeders.

pipplo.habitat: Sandy beaches, tidal flats and inlet shoals in winter.
pipplo.look: Very pale plover on dry sand above the tide line; scan quiet beach stretches and inlets, moving slowly so it does not flush.

pirfly1.habitat: Tropical; an extreme rarity in Florida.
pirfly1.look: A streaked flycatcher with a dark mask near fruiting trees; needs photos.

pitwhy.habitat: Weedy fields in South Florida; a small established population.
pitwhy.look: Male with absurd long tail streamers in breeding season, feeding on grass seeds in open lots; Miami area.

pomjae.habitat: Offshore waters; occasionally visible from beaches and piers in winter.
pomjae.look: Scan beyond the breakers from a pier for a heavy, broad-winged jaeger chasing gulls; pelagic trips are far more reliable.

prawar.habitat: Scrubby fields, young pines, powerline cuts and mangroves in Florida.
prawar.look: Listen for the rising buzzy scale from a young pine or shrub in April; it pumps its tail.

prowar.habitat: Flooded swamp forest, cypress sloughs and river backwaters.
prowar.look: Listen for the loud ringing 'sweet-sweet-sweet' over still water in April; the golden bird sits low over the water near cavities.

purfin.habitat: Woodland edges and feeders in winter; irruptive.
purfin.look: Check feeder finch flocks from November for a raspberry-washed male or a strongly patterned female with a bold eyebrow.

purgal2.habitat: Freshwater marshes with floating vegetation and pickerelweed.
purgal2.look: Walks across lily pads on long yellow legs; scan the edges of marsh pools and listen for cackling.

purmar.habitat: Martin houses and gourds near open water and fields.
purmar.look: Check martin colonies in neighborhoods and parks from March; in July and August evening pre-roost gatherings reach thousands.

purswa3.habitat: Freshwater marshes and retention ponds in South Florida.
purswa3.look: A huge purple gallinule-like bird with a red bill standing in open marsh; often on the edges of stormwater treatment areas.

razorb.habitat: Offshore; rare winter visitor to Southeast coasts in some years.
razorb.look: Scan from jetties and piers in midwinter for a black-and-white diver sitting low; irruption years bring many.

rebmer.habitat: Coastal bays, inlets and large lakes.
rebmer.look: Scan salt water and big reservoirs for slim, shaggy-crested divers in small groups, often fishing in lines.

rebnut.habitat: Pines, hemlocks and spruce; irruptive in winter in the lowlands.
rebnut.look: Tin-horn 'ank-ank' from pine tops in irruption winters; check pines and feeders from October.

rebtro.habitat: Gulf Stream and Caribbean waters; storm stray.
rebtro.look: Pelagic trips and post-hurricane beach checks; a red-billed tropicbird with barred back.

rebwoo.look: Rolling 'churr' call and a red nape; the common woodpecker at feeders.

recpar.habitat: Suburbs of South Florida with established feral flocks.
recpar.look: Listen for raucous flocks of chunky green amazons at dawn and dusk roost flights.

recpoc.look: Drake with a rounded orange-red head and bright red bill, among ornamental waterfowl.

recwoo.habitat: Mature, open longleaf and loblolly pine stands that are burned regularly.
recwoo.look: Find trees with white paint bands and resin-coated trunks; wait near the cluster at dawn as birds leave cavities, calling with a squeaky 'sklit'.

redcro.habitat: Pine stands with heavy cone crops; irregular.
redcro.look: Listen for 'kip-kip' calls overhead near pine cones; flocks feed quietly at the tops of loblolly and white pines.

redegr.habitat: Shallow coastal lagoons and flats in Florida and the Gulf.
redegr.look: Look for the heron running, spinning and canopy-feeding in open shallows; both dark and white morphs occur.

redhea.look: Rafts of diving ducks offshore; look for a round chestnut head and gray body with a blue bill. Compare with Canvasback's sloping head.

redjun.look: Free-roaming chickens of wild type; a crowing rooster in a known feral flock.

redkno.habitat: Sandy beaches and tidal flats, especially at inlets, in migration and winter.
redkno.look: Scan high-tide roosts and inlet flats for chunky gray shorebirds in tight flocks; in May look for rusty breasts.

redpha1.habitat: Offshore waters; onshore only after storms.
redpha1.look: Check beaches, ponds and reservoirs right after hurricanes and strong coastal storms for a swimming shorebird.

reevir1.habitat: Deciduous forest canopy everywhere in summer.
reevir1.look: Endless question-and-answer phrases from the canopy all day; look for a vireo working the undersides of leaves.

refboo.habitat: Tropical seas; a rare stray to Florida coasts.
refboo.look: Check channel markers, piers and buoys for a small booby with red feet; often found roosting on structures.

rehwoo.habitat: Open oak woods, beaver swamps with dead snags, golf courses and pecan groves.
rehwoo.look: Scan standing dead trees in open settings for a bold black-and-white bird with a red head; watch for flycatching sallies from snags.

rengre.habitat: Large reservoirs and coastal waters; a rare winter visitor.
rengre.look: A big, long-necked grebe with a dusky cheek and yellow bill base; scan reservoirs after hard freezes to the north.

renpha.habitat: Offshore and on inland ponds after storms.
renpha.look: A swimming shorebird spinning on a pond or sewage lagoon in late summer and fall, especially after weather systems.

reshaw.habitat: Wet woods, swamps, river bottoms and wooded suburbs.
reshaw.look: Listen for the loud repeated 'kee-ah' in late winter and spring; perches on wires and low limbs along wooded roads.

rethaw.habitat: Fields, highway edges, open woods; perches on poles and tall trees.
rethaw.look: The big hawk on roadside poles; soars with a red tail by late morning.

retloo.habitat: Nearshore ocean and inlets in winter; rare on big reservoirs.
retloo.look: Scan the surf from piers for a slim loon holding its thin bill tilted up; often moving in lines offshore.

rewbla.habitat: Marshes, wet ditches, fields and feeders.
rewbla.look: Conk-la-ree from every cattail in spring; huge mixed flocks in winter fields.

rewbul.habitat: Suburban Miami neighborhoods with fruiting shrubs.
rewbul.look: A small established population around Kendall; look for a crested bird with red cheek spots in fruiting trees.

ribgul.habitat: Parking lots, reservoirs, landfills, beaches, athletic fields.
ribgul.look: The default inland gull in winter; scan large loafing flocks for rarer gulls.

rinduc.habitat: Wooded ponds, beaver ponds, small lakes and reservoir coves.
rinduc.look: The common diving duck of small freshwater; look for the peaked head and white ring near the bill tip, often in tight flocks.

rinphe1.habitat: Farmland; in the Southeast only released birds.
rinphe1.look: Long-tailed gamebird along field edges, usually from a game release.

robgro.habitat: Deciduous woods and feeders in migration; mountain hardwoods in summer.
robgro.look: Check sunflower feeders in late April and early May; the song is a sweet, fast robin from the canopy.

robpoc1.look: Dark duck with a red knobbed bill among ornamental waterfowl.

rocpig.habitat: Cities, bridges, grain elevators and overpasses.
rocpig.look: Flocks on bridges and buildings; worth checking for falcons hunting them.

rolhaw.habitat: Large open fields and marshes in winter; very rare in the Southeast.
rolhaw.look: Scan big fields for a long-winged buteo hovering in place, with dark wrist patches and a white tail base.

rorpar.habitat: Suburbs with palms; small feral populations in Florida.
rorpar.look: Long-tailed green parakeet with a red bill screeching over neighborhoods at dawn.

rosgoo.habitat: Same places as Snow Goose: reservoirs, sod farms, goose flocks on lawns.
rosgoo.look: Scan Snow and Canada Goose flocks for a smaller, round-headed white goose with a stubby bill lacking the dark grin patch; stays close to other geese.

rosspo1.habitat: Shallow coastal lagoons, mangrove pools and impoundments; increasingly inland.
rosspo1.look: Pink birds sweeping bills side to side in shallows; check impoundments and drying ponds in late summer when post-breeding birds wander north.

roster.habitat: Coastal waters and offshore sandbars in Florida and the Keys.
roster.look: Scan tern roosts for a very pale tern with a long tail and mostly dark bill; rare and local.

royter1.habitat: Beaches, inlets and piers; rare inland after storms.
royter1.look: Large orange-billed tern in loafing flocks on beaches; conspicuous year-round on the coast.

rthhum.habitat: Gardens, feeders, flowering edges and woodland openings.
rthhum.look: Put out a feeder and watch; in the wild look at jewelweed, trumpet creeper and salvia patches. Males perch on exposed twigs.

ruckin.habitat: Brushy edges, thickets and conifers in winter.
ruckin.look: Tiny, hyperactive bird flicking its wings constantly in low shrubs; the scolding 'ji-dit' gives it away.

rudduc.habitat: Ponds, sewage lagoons, reservoir coves with still water.
rudduc.look: Compact duck with a stiff tail, usually in tight sleeping rafts in sheltered water; the blue bill appears in spring.

rudtur.habitat: Rocky jetties, shell beaches and wrack lines on the coast.
rudtur.look: Flips seaweed and shells along the tide line; check jetties and piers.

rufhum.habitat: Feeders and flowering shrubs in late fall and winter.
rufhum.look: The most likely winter hummingbird in the Southeast: keep feeders up past October and watch for rusty flanks and a buzzy, aggressive bird.

rusbla.habitat: Flooded woodlands, beaver swamps and wooded wet ditches in winter.
rusbla.look: Walk swamp edges in winter and listen for squeaky, creaking calls; flocks flip leaves in shallow water. Declining, so check wooded wetlands specifically.

sabgul.habitat: Offshore and on inland reservoirs in fall, especially after storms.
sabgul.look: Check reservoirs and sewage ponds in September for a small gull with a striking three-tone wing pattern.

sancra.habitat: Pastures, wet prairie, golf courses and shallow marsh.
sancra.look: Tall gray birds in pairs or family groups in open grass; the rattling bugle carries far. In Florida look on golf courses and roadsides.

sander.habitat: Sandy ocean beaches, running at the edge of the waves.
sander.look: The pale sandpiper chasing waves; large winter flocks on open beaches.

santer1.habitat: Beaches, inlets and sandbars on the coast.
santer1.look: Look for the yellow-tipped black bill among roosting Royal Terns; shaggy crest.

savspa.habitat: Fields, pastures, sod farms and marsh edges in winter.
savspa.look: Common streaky sparrow of open fields; look for a yellow spot before the eye and a short notched tail.

scaibi.habitat: South American; in Florida only escapes or hybrids.
scaibi.look: A scarlet ibis among White Ibis flocks; nearly all are from captivity.

scatan.habitat: Mature deciduous forest in the mountains and Piedmont; canopy in migration.
scatan.look: Listen for the hoarse robin-like song and 'chip-burr' call from high in oaks; the blazing red male hides surprisingly well in leaves.

scnpig1.habitat: Caribbean forest; in Florida an extreme rarity.
scnpig1.look: A large dark pigeon with a scaled nape in tall trees; nearly all reports need documentation.

scoshe1.look: Separated from Cory's by underwing pattern on pelagic trips; not a shore bird.

sctfly.habitat: Open pastures with fences and scattered trees; a rare migrant and winter bird.
sctfly.look: Scan fence lines and wires in open country, especially in late fall; the streamers are obvious even on a distant perch.

sedwre1.habitat: Damp grassy fields, broomsedge and wet meadows in winter.
sedwre1.look: Walk slowly through tall wet grass in winter; it flushes a few feet and drops back in. Listen for dry 'chip' notes.

semplo.habitat: Mudflats, beaches and drawn-down reservoir margins in migration.
semplo.look: Small banded plover running on mud; scan flats at low tide and reservoir shores in August and September.

semsan.habitat: Mudflats, reservoir shores and coastal pools in migration.
semsan.look: The common gray-brown peep of open mud in May and August; black legs and a short straight bill.

shbdow.habitat: Mudflats, coastal pools and flooded fields in migration.
shbdow.look: Feeds with a sewing-machine motion in shallow water; listen for the mellow 'tu-tu-tu' flight call to separate from Long-billed.

sheowl.habitat: Large marshes, airports and grassland in winter.
sheowl.look: Watch big open fields in the last half hour of light for a moth-like owl quartering low; often shares fields with harriers.

shicow.habitat: Feeders and lawns in Florida; rare elsewhere.
shicow.look: Pick through cowbird flocks for a glossy purple-black male with a slimmer bill; listen for a liquid whistled song.

shshaw.habitat: Woodland edges and yards with feeders in winter; ridges in fall migration.
shshaw.look: A small hawk bursting through a feeder area; in fall watch ridgelines on north winds in late September.

shthaw.habitat: Florida woodlands and wetland edges; hunts high over mixed habitat.
shthaw.look: Scan the sky over cypress and hammock edges late in the morning for a buteo soaring very high; both dark and light morphs occur.

shtshe.habitat: Pacific species; extraordinary in the Atlantic.
shtshe.look: Only from exhaustive documentation; not a bird to look for.

smbani.habitat: Brushy fields and scrub in South Florida; now rare.
smbani.look: Groups of floppy black birds with huge bills in low scrub; listen for whining calls. Known sites only.

smbela1.habitat: South American; a one-time stray to the East.
smbela1.look: A drab elaenia with wing bars and a short crest; any record needs extensive documentation.

snakit.habitat: Freshwater marshes and lake edges with apple snails in central and south Florida.
snakit.look: Watch low over marsh vegetation for a slow-flapping dark raptor with a white tail base; perches on low posts eating snails.

snoegr.habitat: Marshes, pond edges, tidal flats and ditches.
snoegr.look: Active white egret stirring the water with yellow feet; often in loose feeding groups.

snogoo.habitat: Large lakes, reservoirs, sod farms and harvested fields; in the Southeast usually a stray with Canada Geese.
snogoo.look: Pick through Canada Goose flocks on lawns and fields for a white (or blue-morph) bird with pink bill and black wingtips; check the biggest open-water roosts at dusk.
snogoo.time: Morning and late afternoon on fields; dusk at roosts

snoowl1.habitat: Beaches, airports and open fields; an irruptive winter rarity.
snoowl1.look: In invasion winters scan dunes, jetties and airport fields for a big white owl sitting on the ground.

snoplo5.habitat: Gulf beaches with dry sand and shell; nests above the wrack line.
snoplo5.look: Tiny pale plover almost invisible on sand; scan protected beach areas in Lee County, watching for movement.

solsan.habitat: Muddy puddles, wooded pond edges and ditches in migration.
solsan.look: Usually alone at small muddy pools; bobs gently and flushes with a high whistle. Check flooded woodland edges in April and August.

sonspa.habitat: Brushy wet edges, ditches and yards.
sonspa.look: Heavily streaked with a central breast spot, pumping its tail in flight; sings from low perches.

sooshe.habitat: Offshore; occasionally visible from shore in late spring.
sooshe.look: Scan from beaches in May and June during onshore winds for an all-dark shearwater with silvery underwings.

sooter1.habitat: Tropical seas; nests in the Dry Tortugas, storm-blown elsewhere.
sooter1.look: After tropical storms check beaches, lakes and reservoirs for a dark-backed tern with a white forehead.

sora.habitat: Freshwater marsh, flooded fields, pond edges with dense vegetation.
sora.look: The whinnying call gives it away; in fall, walk slowly along wet ditches and marsh edges and watch for a chunky bird slipping into cover.

sposan.habitat: Rocky and muddy shorelines of lakes, rivers and ponds.
sposan.look: Walks the water's edge bobbing its tail constantly, then flies off with stiff shallow wingbeats low over water.

sstspa.look: Visit marsh edges at the highest tides in October and November; a sharp-faced sparrow with crisp streaks, pushed up with Nelson's and Seaside sparrows.

stisan.habitat: Shallow freshwater pools and impoundments in migration.
stisan.look: Feeds belly-deep in groups with a deliberate probing motion; check dowitcher and yellowlegs flocks in July to September.

sumtan.habitat: Open oak and pine woods, wooded suburbs.
sumtan.look: Listen for the 'pit-ti-tuck' call from the canopy; a slow robin-like song. Look near wasp nests, which it raids.

surfbi.habitat: Pacific rocky shores; an extraordinary stray to the East.
surfbi.look: A stocky turnstone-like bird on jetties; any report needs photos.

sursco.habitat: Ocean surf line, inlets and large reservoirs after storms.
sursco.look: Scan just beyond the breakers for dark ducks with a white nape and forehead patches on the drake; lines fly low over the water.

swagoo1.habitat: Urban ponds and farmyards; domestic (Chinese goose) stock.
swagoo1.look: Long-necked goose with a knob at the base of the bill, loafing with Canada Geese or tame flocks.

swahaw.habitat: Open fields and prairies; a rare migrant and winter visitor, mostly South Florida.
swahaw.look: Scan plowed fields for a slim buteo with long wings and a dark chest; often perched on the ground or low posts.

swaspa.habitat: Marshes, wet ditches and flooded weedy fields in winter.
swaspa.look: Look low in wet vegetation for a rusty-winged sparrow with a gray face; responds to pishing by climbing a stem.

swathr.habitat: Woodland understory and fruiting shrubs in migration.
swathr.look: Look for a buff-faced thrush in dogwoods and other fruiting trees in late September and early October; a liquid 'whit' call from cover.

swawar.habitat: Dense canebrakes and rhododendron thickets in river bottoms and ravines.
swawar.look: Listen in late April and May for a loud, slurred song like a Louisiana Waterthrush; it stays on the ground in dense cane. Patience and playback restraint required.

swtkit.habitat: River swamps and pine flats in summer; over fields in late July roosts.
swtkit.look: Look up along river corridors from April to August for the forked tail; late-summer roosts gather dozens over pastures in the evening.

tenwar.habitat: Treetops in migration, especially flowering and fruiting trees.
tenwar.look: In fall check mixed flocks for a plain greenish warbler with a pale eyebrow; in spring listen for a staccato three-part trill from the canopy.

towwar.habitat: Western species; a very rare stray in winter.
towwar.look: A yellow-faced warbler with a dark cheek patch in conifers or at a suet feeder in winter; needs photos.

treswa.habitat: Open water, marshes and fields; huge winter flocks in Florida.
treswa.look: Glossy blue-green swallows over water; roost swarms of thousands at dusk over marsh in winter.

triher.habitat: Coastal marshes, mangrove pools and tidal flats.
triher.look: Slim heron dashing and wading belly-deep; white belly separates it from other dark herons.

trokin.habitat: Open areas with scattered trees; a rare stray, mostly Florida and the Gulf coast.
trokin.look: Yellow-bellied kingbird on wires in fall and winter; separate from Western by notched tail and heavy bill, and by the twittering call.

tuftit.look: Loud 'peter-peter' whistle; a core member of mixed flocks.

tunswa.habitat: Large lakes and flooded fields; in the Southeast a scarce winter visitor to reservoirs.
tunswa.look: Scan open water of big reservoirs in midwinter for white swans with black bills; listen for soft hooting from passing flocks at night and dawn.
tunswa.time: Midwinter, morning scans of open water

turvul.habitat: Everywhere; soars over fields, roads and woods.
turvul.look: Rocking flight on raised wings; big roosts on towers at dusk.

uplsan.habitat: Sod farms, airports and short-grass pastures in migration.
uplsan.look: Scan turf farms in April and August for a slender, small-headed sandpiper standing in short grass; listen for the rolling whistle.

vauswi.habitat: Western species; a rare winter stray in the Southeast.
vauswi.look: Check Chimney Swift roosts in late fall and winter for smaller, paler-rumped birds; most records are from known winter roosts.

veery.habitat: Damp deciduous woods in migration; mountain hardwoods in summer.
veery.look: Listen at dusk in May for the spiraling, breathy song; in migration look low in shady woods for a warm brown thrush with faint spotting.

ventro1.look: A large black-and-orange oriole with a bare blue eye patch at a feeder; captive origin.

verfly.habitat: Open country near water: pond edges, pastures with scattered trees; a rare winter visitor.
verfly.look: Scan fence lines and low perches around ponds in winter for a small flycatcher that drops to the ground; females are peachy-bellied.

vesspa.habitat: Short-grass fields, bare margins and gravel roads in winter and migration.
vesspa.look: Scan field edges and dirt roads for a streaky sparrow that flashes white outer tail feathers when it flies.

vigswa.look: Check Tree Swallow flocks for a bird with white wrapping above the eye and onto the rump sides.

virrai.habitat: Freshwater marshes with dense cattails; winters in Southern marshes.
virrai.look: Listen for the 'kiddick' and grunting calls at dusk; stand quietly beside a cattail edge and watch openings in the mud.

wesgre.habitat: Large reservoirs; a very rare stray.
wesgre.look: Long-necked black-and-white grebe far out on big water; check with a scope and compare with loons.

weskin.habitat: Open fields, wires and coastal scrub in fall and winter.
weskin.look: Scan wires along fields and beaches in October and November for a pale gray kingbird with a yellow belly and white tail edges.

wessan.habitat: Tidal flats and beaches; rare inland.
wessan.look: Pick through peep flocks on coastal flats for drooped bills and rusty scapulars; winters on the coast when Semipalmated has gone.

westan.habitat: Feeders and fruiting trees in winter; a rare western stray.
westan.look: Check feeders offering fruit and suet in winter for a yellow tanager with wing bars; the male has a red face.

whbnut.habitat: Mature deciduous woods and oak-rich suburbs.
whbnut.look: Nasal 'yank' calls; walks headfirst down trunks. Scarce in the Coastal Plain, common in the Piedmont and mountains.

whcpig2.habitat: Mangroves and hardwood hammocks in South Florida.
whcpig2.look: Scan treetops and fruiting trees in hammocks; flocks commute between mangrove nesting islands and mainland feeding trees at dawn and dusk.

whcpin.habitat: Ponds and marshes; in the Southeast nearly always an escape.
whcpin.look: Small brown duck with white cheeks and a red bill spot, usually alone among park waterfowl.

whcspa.habitat: Brushy field edges, hedgerows and farmyards in winter.
whcspa.look: Check hedgerows along fields for a tall, clean-breasted sparrow with a striped crown; often with White-throated flocks.

whevir.habitat: Dense thickets, overgrown fields, brushy swamp edges.
whevir.look: Sings a snappy 'quick-with-the-beer-check' from inside thickets; stay still and it will work toward you.

whiibi.habitat: Lawns, marshes, mudflats and ditches in the Coastal Plain and Florida.
whiibi.look: Flocks probing lawns and wet fields; long lines flying to roost at dusk.

whimbr3.habitat: Salt marsh edges, mudflats and beaches, especially with fiddler crabs.
whimbr3.look: Scan the marsh edge at low tide for a large brown shorebird with a decurved bill and striped crown.

whrsan.habitat: Flooded fields and flats in late spring; drawn-down reservoirs in fall.
whrsan.look: A peep with wingtips extending past the tail and a white rump when it flies; late May and October are best.

whtkit.habitat: Open grassland and marsh edges; rare and local in Florida.
whtkit.look: Scan open fields in South Florida for a pale raptor hovering like a kestrel with wings raised.

whtspa.habitat: Thickets, woodland edges and yards in winter.
whtspa.look: Scratching in leaf litter under shrubs; listen for the sweet 'Old Sam Peabody' whistle, even in winter.

whttro.habitat: Gulf Stream waters; onshore only after storms.
whttro.look: Pelagic trips in summer, or a long shot after hurricanes; a white seabird with long tail streamers.

whwdov.habitat: Suburbs and towns, mostly in Florida; feeders and palms.
whwdov.look: Large dove with a white wing stripe; check wires and feeders, and listen for the 'who cooks for you' cooing.

whwsco2.look: Look for the white wing patch when scoters flap or fly; otherwise a dark bulky duck in the surf or on big reservoirs.

wilfly.habitat: Willow thickets, wet meadows and brushy pond edges.
wilfly.look: Listen for the sneezy 'fitz-bew' from the top of a shrub in May and August; silent birds are best left unidentified.

willet1.habitat: Beaches, salt marsh and tidal flats.
