willet1.look: Plain gray shorebird that flashes a bold black-and-white wing pattern when it flies; loud on the marsh in spring.

wilpha.habitat: Shallow freshwater pools and sewage ponds in migration.
wilpha.look: Spins on the water or wades actively; look for a slim pale shorebird with a needle bill in fall at impoundments.

wilplo.habitat: Sandy beaches, tidal flats and shell bars on the coast.
wilplo.look: Look for a heavy-billed plover on the upper beach and flats, often near fiddler crab burrows.

wilsni1.habitat: Wet meadows, muddy ditches and marsh edges in winter.
wilsni1.look: Walk wet field edges and flush them; they zigzag away with a rasping call. Scan muddy margins for a striped back pressed to the ground.

wiltur.habitat: Mixed woods with openings, field edges, pastures and oak forest.
wiltur.look: Scan field edges and dirt roads at dawn as flocks come out to feed; listen for gobbling in spring.
wiltur.time: First hour after sunrise, late afternoon

winwre3.habitat: Root tangles, brush piles and stream banks in moist woods in winter.
winwre3.look: Look low, at the base of fallen trees and along creek banks, for a tiny dark wren bobbing with its tail cocked; the call is a doubled 'chimp-chimp'.

wispet.look: From shore only after storms; otherwise a pelagic trip, where it patters on the surface behind the boat.

wlswar.habitat: Low willow and alder thickets near water in migration.
wlswar.look: A small yellow warbler with a black cap flitting low in wet shrubs, often in September; check pond-edge thickets.

woewar1.habitat: Steep wooded slopes and ravines with dense understory.
woewar1.look: Listen for a dry, fast trill like a Chipping Sparrow from a hillside; it probes dead leaf clusters at mid-height.

wooduc.habitat: Wooded swamps, beaver ponds, slow creeks and lake coves with overhanging trees.
wooduc.look: Approach quietly; they flush with a rising squeal. Scan shaded shorelines, logs and the backs of coves; check nest boxes in spring.
wooduc.time: First hour of light and the last hour before dark

woosto.habitat: Swamps, cypress ponds, roadside ditches and drying wetlands.
woosto.look: Watch for large white birds soaring on thermals late morning; flocks feed in shrinking pools where fish concentrate in the dry season.
woosto.time: Late morning soaring; early morning feeding

woothr.habitat: Mature moist deciduous woods with a shrub layer.
woothr.look: Listen at dawn and dusk from late April for the flute-like 'ee-oh-lay'; forages on the forest floor.

y00475.habitat: Lakes, ponds and reservoirs in winter; marshes year-round in Florida.
y00475.look: Big rafts on open water in winter; check them for ducks and grebes mixed in.

y00478.habitat: Landfills and large reservoir roosts; a rare winter gull.
y00478.look: A pale, round-headed large gull with grayish or white wingtips; sort through Herring Gull roosts at dams.

y00678.habitat: Pastures and prairie in central Florida; occasionally wanders.
y00678.look: Scan fence posts and roadsides in cattle country for a long-legged raptor walking the ground or with vultures at carcasses.

ycnher.habitat: Wooded swamps, tidal creeks and suburban neighborhoods near water; eats crabs and crayfish.
ycnher.look: Look along creek banks and ditches, and under live oaks for nests in spring; often active in daylight, unlike Black-crowned.

yebcha.habitat: Dense briar thickets, clearcuts and overgrown fields.
yebcha.look: Listen for a bizarre jumble of whistles, clucks and caws from a thicket in May; watch for a display flight with dangling legs.
yebcha.time: Early morning, also at night in spring

yebcuc.habitat: Deciduous woods and thickets, especially along rivers and in tent-caterpillar outbreaks.
yebcuc.look: Heard far more than seen: a hollow 'ka-ka-ka-kowlp-kowlp'. Sits still in the canopy; watch for a long-tailed shape sliding through leaves.
yebcuc.time: Morning, and calls on hot humid afternoons

yebfly.habitat: Shady, damp woods and thickets in migration.
yebfly.look: A small, yellow-washed Empidonax low in moist shade; most likely in late May and September. Listen for the soft rising 'chu-wee'.

yebsap.habitat: Woods, orchards and yards in winter; favors maples, hollies and pines.
yebsap.look: Look for neat rows of sap wells on trunks and the mewing call; quiet and easily overlooked on a trunk.

yecpar.habitat: Suburban Florida with fruiting and flowering trees.
yecpar.look: Small green parakeet with yellow wing bars in flocks over Miami and Fort Lauderdale neighborhoods.

yehbla.habitat: Blackbird flocks in fields and marshes; a rare stray.
yehbla.look: Pick through large blackbird and cowbird flocks at feedlots and sod farms for a yellow head; most often in fall.

yehpar.habitat: South Florida suburbs; small feral numbers.
yehpar.look: A large amazon with a yellow head in roost flights; escapes also common.

yelrai.habitat: Damp grassy fields and marsh edges with short dense grass; very secretive.
yelrai.look: Almost never seen without flushing; most records come from rope drags or mowing. Listen at night for ticking clicks like pebbles tapped.

yelwar1.habitat: Willow thickets, streamside shrubs and mangroves.
yelwar1.look: Listen for 'sweet-sweet-sweet-I'm-so-sweet' from willows near water in spring; a bright yellow bird with yellow tail spots.

yerwar.habitat: Wax myrtle, cedars, open woods and fields in winter; everywhere in migration.
yerwar.look: The abundant winter warbler; flocks flash yellow rumps and give a sharp 'check' call in myrtle thickets.

yetvir.habitat: Mature deciduous woods, especially oaks along streams and ridgetops.
yetvir.look: Listen for a slow, hoarse 'three-eight' from high in the canopy; stays up in the big trees.

yetwar.habitat: Tall pines, sycamores and cypress along rivers.
yetwar.look: Listen for a sweet descending series from high pines in March; it creeps along big limbs like a nuthatch.
